core_obligations: Set up the contradiction: let f : U_T -> U_T union {*} be surjective in the model with finite support A, and derive the key support fact that f(x) = y forces y to lie in the definable closure of A union {x} (proof lines 310-319).

Case 1: if y is not below any element of [A], then any failure of x = y would force y to be the minimal point of a cone at an exceptional ramification point of the form x meet a; iterating the same argument for a preimage of x under f produces a contradiction, so x = y (proof lines 321-334).

Case 2: if y is below some element of [A], then either x is also below an element of [A], in which case no new ramification points appear and [A union {x}] = [A] union {x}, or x lies outside and the previous case applies; in both situations x = y (proof lines 336-341).

Conclude: every point outside [A] is fixed, so f maps [A] onto [A] union {*}, which is impossible for a surjection with finite [A]; hence the surjection does not exist and the cardinality lies in Delta_5, while the final clause follows because the tree is not aleph_0-categorical (proof lines 343-347).
proof_roadmap: From the support of f, show each image point lies in the closure of A together with its preimage, and describe that closure (proof lines 310-319).
Run the two cases to prove that f fixes every point outside [A], contradicting surjectivity onto [A] union {*} (proof lines 321-347).
difficulty_reason: The theorem is about the set U_T of nodes of a countable weakly 2-transitive tree together with its symmetric model with finite supports, and it pins the definable cardinality of U_T into the class Delta_5, with the sharper negative statement when the tree has infinitely many ramification orders (statement lines 307-308). The proof takes a surjection onto U_T union {*} with finite support A and shows that every point outside the definable closure of A is fixed, by analysing where an image point can sit relative to A: outside the closure the only possible obstruction is a cone at an exceptional ramification point created by a meet with an element of A, and iterating that obstruction for a preimage produces a contradiction (proof lines 310-341). The step that carries the content is the description of the closure [A union {x}] and the two-case analysis built on it, since it is what forces the fixed-point behaviour; surjectivity then fails against the finiteness of the support. H2.
